slot.brief: Given the electronic configuration of a lanthanide/transition ion, compute its spin-only magnetic moment using √(n(n+2)) BM.

stem: The spin-only magnetic moment (in BM) of Nd$^{3+}$ (atomic number 60) is closest to:

verdicts.working: Nd³⁺ has configuration [Xe]4f³, with 3 unpaired electrons. The spin-only moment is √[n(n+2)] = √15 ≈ 3.87 BM.

working:
Nd$^{3+}$ has electronic configuration [Xe]4f$^3$. Number of unpaired electrons, $n = 3$. Spin-only magnetic moment $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} = \sqrt{3 \times 5} = \sqrt{15} \approx 3.87$ BM.

Independent check: Nd³⁺ has configuration [Xe]4f³, with 3 unpaired electrons. The spin-only moment is √[n(n+2)] = √15 ≈ 3.87 BM.
solution:
Nd$^{3+}$ has configuration $[\mathrm{Xe}]4f^3$, giving $n=3$ unpaired electrons. The spin-only magnetic moment is
$$\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}=\sqrt{3(3+2)}=\sqrt{15}\approx 3.87\ \text{BM}.$$
